text.title: JPA / Hibernate Failure Modes
text.summary: 15 antipatterns observed in real Spring Data JPA + Hibernate deployments. Each pairs symptom + root cause + concrete fix.

antipattern.symptom: Adding an entity to a `Set` triggers infinite recursion and a `StackOverflowError`; or `Set` semantics break (duplicates allowed).
antipattern.root-cause: `@Data` generates `equals`/`hashCode` over all fields, including lazy collections; touching a collection loads it from the DB and recurses.
antipattern.fix: Replace `@Data` with `@Getter @Setter`. Implement `equals`/`hashCode` manually over a business key per `business-key-equality` rule.

antipattern.symptom: Two unpersisted entities compare equal and collapse into one element of a `Set`/`Map`; after flush the same object stops matching its earlier hash bucket.
antipattern.root-cause: `equals`/`hashCode` written over the DB-assigned `@Id`, typically via Lombok `@EqualsAndHashCode(of = "id")`. Before insert `id` is `null`, so every transient instance is equal to every other; after insert the hash changes.
antipattern.fix: Use an externally-assigned UUID or a business key per `business-key-equality`, or Mihalcea's type-plus-UUID pattern that stays stable across the transient→managed transition.

antipattern.symptom: Query returns 5MB JSON or throws `MultipleBagFetchException`; profile shows multi-million-row Cartesian join.
antipattern.root-cause: Author set `FetchType.EAGER` on an association "to be safe"; combined with another EAGER collection it explodes.
antipattern.fix: Switch all associations to LAZY; do per-query `JOIN FETCH` or `@EntityGraph` when callers actually need the data.

antipattern.symptom: Deleting an `OrderLine` cascades to the parent `Order` and wipes the entire order plus all sibling lines.
antipattern.root-cause: `CascadeType.ALL` on a `@ManyToOne` propagates persist/merge/remove up the ownership chain — semantically backwards.
antipattern.fix: Remove cascade from `@ManyToOne`. Cascade is only appropriate from parent to children on `@OneToMany`.

antipattern.symptom: Deploy aborts with `SchemaManagementException: missing column ...` or — worse — `ddl-auto=update` silently alters the prod schema.
antipattern.root-cause: Entity diff merged without a paired Flyway migration. CI hides it because tests run `ddl-auto=create`; only the production deploy, running `validate`, fails.
antipattern.fix: Enforce `ddl-auto=validate` in prod profile; gate PRs on a `validate-paired-migration.py` script that fails if an entity diff lands without a `db/migration/V*.sql` change. `ddl-auto=update` is never the fix: it cannot drop a column, cannot rename one, and has no rollback path — schema change belongs in a reviewed Flyway/Liquibase migration with a documented rollback.

antipattern.symptom: Bulk update reports `n` rows updated; subsequent `findById` returns the pre-update entity; logic that depends on the new state breaks silently.
antipattern.root-cause: `@Modifying` JPQL bypasses Hibernate's first-level cache; without `clearAutomatically`, stale entities linger in the persistence context.
antipattern.fix: Annotate `@Modifying(clearAutomatically = true, flushAutomatically = true)` on every bulk update/delete repository method.

antipattern.symptom: Repository test suite takes 90 s to boot; CI flakes when the full context cache exceeds the JVM heap.
antipattern.root-cause: Author used `@SpringBootTest` for what should be a repository-only test, loading the entire web + security context.
antipattern.fix: Switch to `@DataJpaTest` + Testcontainers; reserve `@SpringBootTest` for cross-layer integration tests where the full stack is the SUT.

antipattern.symptom: `spring.jpa.open-in-view=true` (the Spring Boot default). Lazy collections accessed during JSON serialisation fire queries on the request thread; p99 latency inflates and `LazyInitializationException` never surfaces in development.
antipattern.root-cause: OSIV keeps the `EntityManager` session open across the whole HTTP lifecycle including the view/serialisation layer, masking N+1 in dev and exhausting the connection pool under production pressure.
antipattern.fix: Set `spring.jpa.open-in-view=false` in every profile and add a CI check that fails if the property is missing or true. Eager-load required associations inside the service via `JOIN FETCH` / `@EntityGraph` and map to DTOs before returning.

antipattern.symptom: Service returns an entity; the controller or `@RestController` serialiser walks a nested collection; `LazyInitializationException` fires.
antipattern.root-cause: The Hibernate session closes when the service transaction commits; accessing `order.getItems()` afterwards queries a closed session.
antipattern.fix: Either load the association via `JOIN FETCH` / `@EntityGraph` in the repository method, or map to a DTO inside the transactional service so the controller never touches the entity graph.

antipattern.symptom: A list endpoint loads 100 orders; iterating `order.items` triggers 100 extra `SELECT * FROM items WHERE order_id = ?`. The endpoint takes 4 s.
antipattern.root-cause: `findAll()` returned entities and the caller iterated collections without `JOIN FETCH`. LAZY is the correct default; the missing piece is the explicit fetch plan.
antipattern.fix: Add a repository method with `@Query("SELECT o FROM Order o JOIN FETCH o.items")` or an `@EntityGraph`, or project straight to a DTO carrying only the required fields. Enable `hibernate.generate_statistics` and review the query count per test.

antipattern.symptom: `@OneToMany(cascade = CascadeType.ALL, orphanRemoval = true)` on `Customer.orders`. Deleting a customer wipes their order history including paid invoices — a compliance and customer-trust event.
antipattern.root-cause: `CascadeType.ALL` applied reflexively without analysing ownership. With `orphanRemoval = true`, removing a child from the collection deletes a row that another aggregate may still reference.
antipattern.fix: Narrow the cascade set (often `PERSIST, MERGE` only) and write the Javadoc justification required by `justified-cascade-fetch`. Use `orphanRemoval` only where the child genuinely cannot exist without the parent.

antipattern.symptom: `NoSuchElementException: No value present` in the logs with no entity id, no type and no request context.
antipattern.fix: Use `findById(id).orElseThrow(() -> new NotFoundException("User " + id + " not found"))` so the message names the aggregate and the exception handler can map it to a 404.

antipattern.symptom: Bidirectional association serialises to infinite recursion, or a JSON response leaks a password column.
antipattern.root-cause: The entity was handed to Jackson instead of a DTO; the back-reference re-enters the parent forever and every mapped column is exposed by default.
antipattern.fix: Serialise through DTOs per `dto-projection-in-controllers`. `@JsonIgnore` on the back-reference is a patch, not the boundary.

antipattern.symptom: A `@Query(nativeQuery = true)` built by string concatenation over a request parameter; a crafted filter value returns rows from another tenant.
antipattern.root-cause: JPQL and native queries concatenated instead of parameterised, usually to implement dynamic filtering.
antipattern.fix: Use named parameters (`:name`) exclusively; for dynamic filtering use `JpaSpecificationExecutor` / Criteria API, which is type-safe. Treat every `nativeQuery = true` as a human review checkpoint.

antipattern.symptom: Intermittent `IllegalStateException: Session/EntityManager is closed`, or entities from one request visible in another.
antipattern.root-cause: `EntityManager` injected into a singleton that outlives the request instead of being scoped to a transaction.
antipattern.fix: Inject `EntityManager` only via `@PersistenceContext` into beans used inside a transaction, or go through the repository. Never cache it on a long-lived field.
